cards.front: Recall a key point about Training Methods
cards.back: A series of exercises performed one after another at different stations. Each station targets a different muscle group or fitness component, with a set time or number of reps at each station, followed by a short rest before moving to the next.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Training Methods
cards.back: Exercising at a steady, moderate intensity for a sustained period without rest breaks. The heart rate is maintained at 60-80% of maximum heart rate throughout the session.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Training Methods
cards.back: "Speed play" - a form of continuous training where the intensity varies throughout the session. The performer alternates between fast and slow running (or other activities) over varying terrain, without structured rest periods.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Training Methods
cards.back: Alternating periods of high-intensity exercise with periods of rest or low-intensity recovery. HIIT (High Intensity Interval Training) involves very intense bursts (85-95% max HR) with short recovery periods.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Training Methods
cards.back: Using resistance (free weights, machines, body weight) to develop muscular strength, endurance and hypertrophy. The programme can be adapted by changing reps, sets, weight and rest periods.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Training Methods
cards.back: Exercises that involve rapid, powerful movements using the stretch-shortening cycle of muscles. The muscle is stretched (eccentric contraction) then immediately contracted (concentric contraction) to produce an explosive movement.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Training Methods
cards.back: Stretching a muscle to its maximum length and holding the position still for a period of time (typically 10-30 seconds). This develops flexibility at a joint.

cards.front: What should you know about pe exam tips — training methods?
cards.back: 1. For Training Methods questions, use subject-specific terminology precisely 2. Support every point with specific evidence or examples 3. Show balanced analysis — consider different perspectives before reaching a conclusion 4. Link your understanding of Training Methods to real-world contexts where possible 5. For longer answers, plan your response to address all parts of the question

cards.front: What does Can target multiple fitness components in one session mean?
cards.back: Requires equipment and space for multiple stations

cards.front: What does Varied - reduces tedium (addresses the T in SPORT) mean?
cards.back: May not develop one specific component enough for elite performers

cards.front: What does Can be easily adapted for different sports and fitness levels mean?
cards.back: Can be difficult to monitor technique at all stations simultaneously

cards.front: What does Suitable for groups and team training mean?
cards.back: Rest periods may not be long enough for full recovery between stations

cards.front: What does Excellent for developing cardiovascular endurance mean?
What does Easy to plan and monitor - just maintain pace mean?
cards.back: Does not improve anaerobic fitness or speed

cards.front: What does Requires minimal equipment mean?
cards.back: High impact (running) can cause injury to joints
